subject.title: [Feature]: Discord self-profile updates (strict bot-only scope for nickname/avatar/status)

question: Should Discord expose bot self-profile mutation, and should that surface reuse the existing plugin-owned `set-profile` action or introduce a Discord-specific `self-profile` action with its own gate and result contract?
rationale: The current code lacks the requested surface, and implementing it creates a bot-credential-backed identity mutation path plus public config/API behavior that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow profile action
options.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned, default-off profile update action with strict owner/self checks, explicit account routing, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof; prefer reusing `set-profile` unless maintainers choose a new name.

options.title: Narrow to presence only
options.body: Reject nickname/avatar mutation for now and route the status/activity subset through the existing `set-presence` or the related dynamic presence API discussion.

options.title: Defer identity mutation
options.body: Keep bot identity changes manual or external until maintainers define a broader Discord identity model across self-profile, per-binding identity, and webhooks.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow profile action
recommendation.body: Add a Discord plugin-owned, default-off profile update action with strict owner/self checks, explicit account routing, avatar validation, docs, regression tests, and live Discord proof; prefer reusing `set-profile` unless maintainers choose a new name.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the closest merged Discord presence-health work and that PR explicitly scoped out self-profile behavior.
